value: Seed germination differed significantly among 0, 15 and 62.5 µmol m−2 s−1 photon irradiance treatments

source.authors: Lai L, Chen L, Jiang L, Zhou J, Zheng Y, Shimizu H
source.title: Seed germination of seven desert plants and implications for vegetation restoration

where: Results, Effects of photon irradiance on seed germination (paragraph before Fig 1)
quote: The seed germination of C. microphylla and Melilotus suaveolens was sensitive to light, and differed significantly among the 0, 15 and 62.5 µmol m−2 s−1 photon irradiance treatments.
conditions: Horqin Sandy Land seeds collected October 2004, stored at 4°C for 12 months; no scarification; 25/15°C day/night; relative humidity 60:50%; darkness or 14-h light/10-h dark; 30 days; five replicates of 25 seeds per treatment. Five irradiances tested: 0, 15, 62.5, 250, 1000 µmol m−2 s−1. Daily inspections under dim fluorescent light (10 µmol m−2 s−1).
method: Radicle emergence; final germination percentage under controlled photon irradiance
note: Only Melilotus suaveolens is logged; shared sentence also names C. microphylla. No numerical percentage is inferred from a plot. Targeted Methods and Results read in published XML via Europe PMC (PMC4940479), also compared with publisher page; CC BY 4.0.
